title: Forty 11-adic candidates on the mixed genus-2 bridge D for G1(15,8), tagged by Omega class
supersedes: the first edition produced by build_candidates_table.py; the two extractions were cross-checked and agree on all 40 signatures
status_of_this_file: EXTRACTION + CROSS-CHECKS ONLY. It proves nothing about D(Q). A candidate that is not removed is NOT a rational point.

curve.run_status_string: completed; full certificate still requires audit

omega_ordering.index_formula: index = 6*i7 + 2*i17 + i23, where i7 indexes [-2, -4/3], i17 indexes [-2, 0, 2], i23 indexes [2, 4/3]
omega_ordering.distinctness_evidence: Qp(11,30): all 66 pairwise differences have valuation in [1, 3], hence nonzero

residue_discs.why_only_two: local_discs_11.py/json, reproduced here: of the 12 projective x in P^1(F_11), only x = 0 and x = infinity make all five square forms of G1(15,8) squares mod 11; in every excluded case the offending value is a unit non-residue (no zeros occur), so the form is a non-square in Q_11 for the whole disc.
residue_discs.CAVEAT: The run therefore covers only 4 of the 12 residue discs of D(F_11). This is sound for the five-squareness locus and for nothing else: the output is NOT a determination of D(Q).

known_rational_points_control.note: These four points must survive any sieve built from this table. A sieve that removes one of them is broken and must be reported, not tuned.
known_rational_points_control.nine_cell_status: both lifts are magic squares of squares but DEGENERATE (only three distinct cell values); see qc_precision_audit.json

orbit_structure_over_E1_x_E2.why: phi1_X = a6*x^2 and phi2_X = a0/x^2 depend on x only through x^2, and phi1_X * phi2_X = a0*a6 identically. sigma: x -> -x fixes both X and flips the sign of phi2_Y; iota: y -> -y flips both Y. So the group <sigma, iota> ~ (Z/2)^2 acts simply transitively on the four sign choices over one pair (X1, X2). Verified numerically below.
orbit_structure_over_E1_x_E2.consequence_for_the_sieve: the 40 candidates carry only 10 distinct pairs (phi1_X, phi2_X); a sieve that works with X-coordinates alone sees 10 classes, not 40, and each class has a single well-defined Omega index.
